assessment.nobel_worthiness: A clean discovery-and-prediction pair: Kane and Mele's Z2 time-reversal-invariant topological insulator theory, with Molenkamp's group providing the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall edge channels in HgTe/CdTe wells. It created a whole field of topological materials with spectroscopic and transport signatures that experimentalists, including electron-microscopy and surface-analysis groups, use routinely. Strongly fits the 'discovery or invention' criterion.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical identification; the HgTe/CdTe prediction by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the Konig et al. experiment complicate credit, but within the supplied names Kane, Mele and Molenkamp form a defensible theory-plus-experiment trio. Other contributors (Zhang, Bernevig, Moore, Balents, Fu, Hasan) are outside the credited strings and I note the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of independent confirmation in HgTe, InAs/GaSb and many three-dimensional materials; interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely to somewhat overdue.
uncertainties: Overlap with a separate topological-insulator and quantum-anomalous-Hall candidate and the surrounding priority questions (Zhang, Bernevig, Fu, Moore, Balents, Hasan) mean the cleanest configuration is not settled.
I have not independently verified the details of early HgTe transport priority; I rely on general knowledge.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Bistritzer-MacDonald flat-band prediction at the magic angle, followed by the 2018 observation of correlated insulator and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene, opened moire quantum materials. It combines a clear theoretical mechanism with a dramatic, controllable experiment, and has spawned a large body of work on tunable correlated and topological states.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the quantitative prediction; Jarillo-Herrero's group carried out the decisive experiments (with Cao and co-workers, who are not in the supplied credit list). The three supplied names can support a fair prize, though I would regard Jarillo-Herrero and MacDonald as the core pair and the inclusion of Bistritzer versus experimental co-authors as unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Experiments are independently reproduced across many groups and structures, but the field is still evolving; microscopic origin of superconductivity and some inhomogeneity issues (twist-angle disorder, as seen in scanning probe and TEM-type imaging) remain debated. Recognition may be slightly early but not premature.
uncertainties: Origin of the superconductivity is not settled.
Credit for the experimental discovery involves early-career co-authors outside the credited names.
Twist-angle inhomogeneity complicates the cleanest reading of some reports.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection of single NV centers in diamond and subsequent coherent control at room temperature created a robust solid-state spin platform that is now used for nanoscale magnetic, electric and thermal sensing and in quantum networks. It is a concrete instrument-style invention with clear impact across physics, chemistry and biology, and relates closely to the single-defect characterization I know from microscopy.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup and Jelezko made the decisive early observation of single-NV optical detection and magnetic resonance and the coherent control; Lukin's contribution is important for quantum registers, sensing proposals and error correction but is a distinct, later strand. I would propose the two experimental pioneers and leave Lukin out of this configuration.
assessment.maturity: Strong independent confirmation and widespread adoption for more than a decade; applications such as nanoscale NMR and biological sensing continue to mature, while some headline claims remain at proof-of-principle level.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should centre on the sensing application or on the spin-qubit physics is open.
Priority relationships to other early single-defect studies are not independently verified by me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Reproducible room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions in 1995 turned a laboratory curiosity into the basis for read heads and magnetic random-access memory. It combines a well-defined physical effect with a large technological consequence, and the materials and interface quality questions (barrier structure, oxygen content, interface sharpness) are exactly where electron microscopy matters.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported large room-temperature TMR in 1995, which is a credible two-person attribution. Parkin's contribution to MgO-barrier and optimised structures, and Julliere's earlier low-temperature work, are separate threads; the supplied three-name list would require choosing between the discovery and the engineering optimisation.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature and commercially realised; the physical picture, including coherent tunnelling in MgO, is well confirmed. Overshadowed in part by the 2007 giant magnetoresistance prize, which may reduce appetite for a closely related spintronics award.
uncertainties: Closeness to the 2007 GMR prize may be viewed as incremental.
Division of credit between the 1995 discovery and the later MgO optimisation is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: High-resolution ARPES transformed the direct measurement of electronic band structure, Fermi surfaces, gaps and many-body self-energies in correlated materials, especially cuprate superconductors. This is a measurement invention with decades of scientific consequence, and as a spectroscopy-and-imaging person I value that methodological advance.
assessment.attribution: Campuzano and Shen are the most identifiable leaders for the cuprate application, but ARPES instrumentation also rests on many others (for example Hufner, Dessau, Damascelli, Lanzara and synchrotron beamline developers) who are not credited here; the claim of decisive credit for two names is therefore somewhat fragile.
assessment.maturity: Technique is thoroughly mature and used worldwide; however the physical interpretation of cuprate spectra (pseudogap, kinks) remains debated, which makes the discovery strand less crisp than the methodological one.
uncertainties: Whether the prize target is the technique or a specific physical discovery is unclear.
Broad contributor base makes a two-person attribution uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's proposal of magic-wavelength optical lattice clocks and Ye's realisation of record-stability clocks created the most precise measurement devices yet built, with consequences for redefinition of the second, tests of fundamental constants, geodesy and relativity. Clear invention with a well-defined function.
assessment.attribution: Katori is the originator of the lattice-clock concept and early demonstrations, and Ye led the push to extreme accuracy; two names suffice. Other clock groups (for example ion-clock work) are recognised in a prior prize, so overlap with earlier awards for ion-based and comb contributions needs attention.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, independently reproduced across several institutions, and metrologically adopted; the timing is good, although a redefinition of the SI second has not yet happened.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier prizes on frequency combs and ion traps may make the committee wary.
I have not verified the latest accuracy records and international redefinition timeline.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2012 measurement of a nonzero theta-13 by Daya Bay and RENO completed the three-flavour mixing picture and enabled CP-violation searches; it was an experimentally decisive discovery with a clear observable, reactor antineutrino disappearance, large statistics and strong controls.
assessment.attribution: Daya Bay and RENO spokespersons Wang, Luk and Kim are identifiable leaders, but Double Chooz and T2K contributed independent evidence, and large-collaboration credit is hard to allocate to individuals. The supplied names do not include Double Chooz leadership, which complicates fairness.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by multiple experiments and now a precision parameter; recognition is timely though close in topic to the 2015 neutrino-oscillation prize, which could lower priority.
uncertainties: Individual attribution within large collaborations is difficult.
Close to the 2015 oscillation prize in subject matter.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hosono's 2006 and 2008 discovery of superconductivity in LaFeAsO(F) and the rapid raising of Tc above 50 K in iron pnictides established the second family of high-temperature superconductors, an important materials discovery whose structure-property relations rely on crystallographic and microscopy characterisation.
assessment.attribution: Hosono made the originating discovery; Zhao's and Chen's groups raised the transition temperature rapidly and established the family. Three names are defensible, with Hosono central, but the credit among many groups in 2008 is contested.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed with a large literature; however, the pairing mechanism is unresolved and practical impact has remained modest relative to cuprates, so recognition may be premature if the committee wants mechanistic understanding.
uncertainties: Competing priorities among groups in early 2008.
